decisions.reason: Step 3.1 supplied only successive existential Bolzano–Weierstrass extractions, not a choice function on the changing subsequences. The proof explicitly promises no DC, so this is an unlicensed recursive inference. A deterministic left-first infinite-occupancy bisection with least increasing indices now supplies a unique extraction map; recursion and the diagonal tail argument require no choice. The Fourier N^-2 tail and Parseval still prove L2 compactness, and the Poincare, separability and Hilbert arguments retain their hypotheses.

F4 attributes the diagonal extraction to AC_omega although the available subsequences depend on previous selections. Replaced that unlicensed choice inference by an explicit deterministic interval-bisection and least-index extraction, recursively iterated over the fixed countable rational test span. Averaging gives sampled norm convergence for every finite product test (expand all cross terms); the limiting rational-linear functional extends continuously and real-linearly, and Riesz plus the two fixed-test error bounds establishes the full stated convergence.

The original Statement allowed zero or negative scales tending to zero, whereas the explicitly cited two-scale definition has domain epsilon_n>0. Added positivity to the Statement, Given and F3; no claimed positive-scale conclusion is weakened. Weak/strong extraction uses the repaired cube compactness and two-scale compactness, finite component extraction and the published deterministic separable-Hilbert lemma. Divergence-free cosine/sine tests identify all nonzero Fourier modes as parallel to their frequencies; the weighted coefficient estimate constructs the real mean-zero H1 potential with integrable slice norm.

F4 incorrectly attributes divergence-free Fourier orthogonality to the basis/Parseval theorem. This is a nonfatal missing elementary derivation: sine and cosine of each nonzero integer frequency are legitimate mean-zero periodic cell tests, giving k dot qhat(k)=0. Added that calculation and restricted F4 to the actual Fourier interface. Integer-frequency dilation preserves orthogonality, the affine L2 bound passes the identity to the flux, and the translated-cell partition gives the exact mean A*p. The minimizer remains unique by ellipticity and mean-zero normalization.

A1 misdescribes the Countable Choice definition as a statement about Fourier representatives. This is nonfatal: coefficients are representative-invariant integrals, and the Fourier theorem already records precisely the AC_omega assumption. Corrected A1 to that actual use. The cell equation tested with character real/imaginary parts proves frequency orthogonality; the displayed antisymmetric coefficient formula gives divergence q and a weighted square-summability bound. Explicit L2 limits of symmetric sums and derivatives now justify the periodic H1 reconstruction, zero mean, realness and norm bound.

F4 overstates the cited Statement by attributing a specific primitive construction and multidimensional lifting to a supplier whose stated interface gives a one-dimensional cell solution and harmonic mean flux. The original lifting calculation was elementary and sound, so this is a nonfatal citation-interface defect. F4 now states only that interface. Step 1.1 lifts its unique solution via smooth periodic approximants with equal H1 norm differences, applies the one-dimensional cell equation to each smooth slice, and averages the stated flux. Transverse correctors vanish by periodic slice integration, giving all displayed columns.
